scope: Proposition 4.3 (Conditional next-pin first moment) of the manuscript “Spontaneous magnetization in the quantum Heisenberg ferromagnet” (preprints/Spontaneous-magnetization-in-the-quantum-Heisenberg-ferromagnet-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 271 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8c9083e5eb7a9d6f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 20. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let V = J ⊔ Q be a finite set with J ̸= ∅. Let Π be a random permutation matrix satisfying (4.6), and put K = EΠ. Let GJ be the event that every cycle of Π meets J. On GJ , let Σ be the column-forward permutation matrix of the next visit to J at positive time along the cycles. Then P(GJ ) = det(I − KQQ). (4.7) If this probability is positive, KQQ is transient and E[Σ | GJ ] = H := KJJ + KJQ(I − KQQ)−1 KQJ . (4.8) The matrix H is the first positive J-hitting kernel for the Markov chain with transition matrix K, using independent transitions on successive steps. More strongly, for every complex J × J matrix W, E[det(I − WΣ) | GJ ] = det(I − WH). (4.9) An empty Q is allowed, with determinant of the empty matrix equal to one and the Schur correction in (4.8) equal to zero.
